claude_envelope.result: {"verdict":"CHANGES_REQUESTED","lens":"safety_bypass","summary":"Slice 020H.3 introduces 1 CRIT, 3 MAJ, 2 MIN, and 2 nit safety/bypass findings. CRIT-SAFE-001: the workflow fires on push:tags — the tag already exists on the remote when the workflow starts. The workflow cannot prevent the tag from existing; it can only annotate and fail the run. Both the workflow header ('Refuses a tag-cut on v*') and VERSIONING.md ('the gate refuses a tag-cut') make an architecturally false claim about the security property. The dry_run workflow_dispatch is the real pre-flight but operator discipline is the only enforcement — nothing prevents skipping it. MAJ-SAFE-002 (compounding): the D-030 tag-protection ruleset blocks deletion/update with bypass_actors:[], so a bad tag that the workflow correctly annotates as violating the ramp CANNOT be deleted even by the admin. The bad tag is permanent on the remote and adopters who fetch it get the bad release — there is no documented recovery path. MAJ-SAFE-003: .scp/** is absent from CODEOWNERS; if a future SCP-self rule-config.yaml is added it becomes load-bearing for the release gate's expired-config check but is unprotected, allowing it to be merged without CODEOWNERS-gated review. MAJ-SAFE-004: deprecations.yaml can be tampered in two ways — (a) changing announced_release to a prior-major version converts a same-major ramp violation (0 minor delta) into the 'major-bump removal accepted' fast path, silently bypassing the one-release window; (b) changing target_release to a future tag removes the entry from the candidate filter for the current cut, letting a surface be removed with no ramp check applied. Both are CODEOWNERS-protected but self-mergeable in single-operator mode. MIN-SAFE-005: the expired-config check uses datetime.date.today() with strict less-than comparison, while policy-check.yml uses timezone-aware datetime.now(timezone.utc) with >= comparison; on the expiry day itself, release-gate considers the entry NOT expired but policy-check does, creating a one-day divergence window. MIN-SAFE-006: pyyaml and jsonschema are pip-installed with version-only pins (no --require-hashes), unlike the OPA/Conftest/Regal SHA256 lockfile pattern. nit-SAFE-007: concurrency group expression for workflow_dispatch always evaluates to refs/heads/main (github.ref is always set); the || github.event.inputs.dry_run_tag branch is dead code. nit-SAFE-008: DISPATCH-NOTE 'Out of scope' section omits the post-push observation-only limitation, which should be disclosed per §4.3 disclosure contract.","findings":[{"id":"CRIT-SAFE-001","severity":"CRIT","claim":"The workflow fires on push:tags AFTER the tag has been pushed to the remote. GitHub Actions cannot block a push:tags event — the tag already exists on the remote when the first workflow step runs. The claim in the workflow header ('Refuses a tag-cut on v*') and in VERSIONING.md ('Machine enforcement: ...refuses the tag-cut (SCP-EREL-001)') is architecturally false. The workflow can annotate and fail the run, but the tag is live, the release is visible, and any adopter who fetches the tag immediately after push receives the non-compliant release. The workflow_dispatch dry_run path is the real pre-flight mechanism, but operator discipline is the only enforcement — nothing in the system prevents skipping the dry_run before tagging.","evidence":"release-gate.yml lines 35-38: trigger is 'push: tags: [\"v*\"]'. GitHub's push:tags event fires after the ref has been created on the remote, after which it cannot be cancelled by a workflow. lines 96-108 (Resolve candidate tag): tag is extracted from GITHUB_REF which already reflects the live remote state. VERSIONING.md line 130-131: 'Machine enforcement: .github/workflows/release-gate.yml runs on every push: tags: [\"v*\"] ...It refuses the tag-cut (SCP-EREL-001)'. DISPATCH-NOTE.md acceptance criterion (iii): 'All refusals emit ::error::title=SCP-EREL-001'. Neither document acknowledges that the refusal annotation is post-hoc, not pre-emptive. The only pre-emptive path is the operator voluntarily running 'gh workflow run release-gate.yml -f dry_run_tag=v1.1.0' before tagging — VERSIONING.md documents this guidance at line 141 but there is no machine enforcement of the discipline.","impact":"An operator (or attacker with push-to-tags access) who skips the dry_run pre-flight and pushes a tag that violates the deprecation ramp gets: the tag exists on the remote, the workflow fails and emits SCP-EREL-001 annotations, and adopters who fetch the tag within the window between tag push and workflow-fail notification receive the non-compliant release. The failure notification is a GitHub Actions email/notification, not a blocking gate. Adopter repos with Renovate configured to watch this tag series will see the tag and may open an upgrade PR. The documentation misleads adopters (and future maintainers) about the strength of the enforcement guarantee, causing over-reliance on a property the mechanism does not provide.","mitigation":"(1) Correct VERSIONING.md and the release-gate.yml header comment to state accurately: the gate detects and annotates ramp violations; it does not prevent the tag from being created. The pre-emptive enforcement is the dry_run discipline. (2) Promote the dry_run pre-flight to a documented mandatory step in VERSIONING.md's 'Deprecation ramp' section alongside the tag-cut instruction — 'Before cutting any v* tag, ALWAYS run: gh workflow run release-gate.yml -f dry_run_tag=<tag>; wait for the run to complete with exit 0 before pushing the tag.' (3) Document the recovery procedure for a bad tag (see CRIT-SAFE-001 + MAJ-SAFE-002 for the interlock with tag-protection). These are documentation changes only; no workflow code change is needed for this finding. The enforcement model is defensible as long as the claim matches reality."},{"id":"MAJ-SAFE-002","severity":"MAJ","claim":"The D-030 tag-protection ruleset (scp-tag-protection-v) blocks deletion, non_fast_forward, and update on v* tags with bypass_actors:[] and enforcement:active. This means even the repo admin cannot delete a tag once created. If an operator erroneously pushes a tag that violates the ramp (e.g., skipped the dry_run pre-flight), the release-gate workflow correctly fails and annotates the violation, but the bad tag CANNOT be deleted to contain the damage. There is no documented recovery path for this scenario.","evidence":"branch-protection.md lines 113-127: scp-tag-protection-v ruleset; 'deletion / non_fast_forward / update blocked'; 'bypass_actors: []' (all actors including admin blocked). docs/DECISIONS.md D-030: 'a single GitHub admin (@jrnb2024) can disable these via repo Settings; quarterly review cadence'. release-gate.yml has no step that attempts tag deletion (it lacks write permissions: permissions.contents=read at line 47). The workflow cannot delete the tag even if it wanted to. No step in any workflow file creates an issue, posts a comment, or takes recovery action on violation detection — the only output is ::error:: annotations and a non-zero exit code. DISPATCH-NOTE.md 'Out of scope' section does not mention the bad-tag-is-permanent scenario.","impact":"A tag-protection + post-push workflow creates a compound failure mode: (1) operator pushes v1.1.0 while skipping dry_run; (2) workflow fails, annotates ramp violation; (3) tag v1.1.0 exists, is visible to adopters, Renovate opens upgrade PRs; (4) operator cannot delete v1.1.0 without first disabling the ruleset via GitHub Settings; (5) there is no documented procedure for step (4), nor an acknowledgement that it is required. This scenario is made more likely by the misleading 'refuses the tag-cut' documentation (CRIT-SAFE-001) — an operator who believes the gate is pre-emptive may not think to run dry_run. The D-030 ruleset design rationale (preventing accidental force-push) is sound in isolation, but its interaction with the post-push gate is undocumented.","mitigation":"(1) Add a 'Bad-tag recovery procedure' subsection to VERSIONING.md and docs/security/branch-protection.md: 'If a tag is pushed that fails the release-gate check: (a) do NOT attempt to delete or force-push the tag — it is immutable per D-030; (b) cut a corrected v<X>.<Y+1>.0 (next minor) that satisfies the ramp; the bad tag remains but is superseded; (c) add a release note on the bad tag's GitHub release page documenting the violation and pointing to the corrected tag.' (2) Consider documenting the temporary-ruleset-disable path as an emergency escape: 'In exceptional cases where tag deletion is required, the operator must file a D-NNN decision before disabling the ruleset, perform the deletion, re-enable the ruleset, and record the D-NNN in the next quarterly branch-protection review.' No workflow code change needed."},{"id":"MAJ-SAFE-003","severity":"MAJ","claim":".scp/** is absent from CODEOWNERS. The release-gate workflow's expired-config check at lines 213-258 reads .scp/rule-config.yaml when present. Once any SCP-self rule-config is added (currently absent, so the check is silently skipped), the file becomes load-bearing for the gate: an entry with disable:true and expires_at in the future could suppress a policy rule at tag-cut time. Without CODEOWNERS coverage, a PR adding or modifying .scp/rule-config.yaml is not routed to @jrnb2024 for mandatory review.","evidence":"CODEOWNERS full file reviewed: paths covered include policies/**, schemas/**, lib/**, .github/**, tests/**, renovate/**, scripts/**, vendor/**, version-manifest.json, /CODEOWNERS, docs/CODEOWNERS, and several docs/** subtrees. No .scp/** or .scp/rule-config.yaml entry exists. release-gate.yml line 213: 'if [ ! -f .scp/rule-config.yaml ]; then echo \".scp/rule-config.yaml absent on SCP repo; expired-config check skipped\"; exit 0; fi'. policy-check.yml SCP_RULE_CONFIG_PATH defaults to .scp/rule-config.yaml (line 35). schema at schemas/rule-config.schema.json is covered by schemas/** but the data file at .scp/ is not. The CODEOWNERS header comment (lines 1-31) shows extensive reasoning about why each path was added; .scp/** is not mentioned, suggesting it was overlooked rather than intentionally excluded.","impact":"If .scp/rule-config.yaml is added to the SCP repo (a legitimate future action as SCP self-dogfoods rule governance), any subsequent PR that modifies it to extend expires_at dates, add new disable entries, or remove existing entries can be merged without @jrnb2024 CODEOWNERS review in single-operator mode (though in single-operator mode all merges are self-approved). More critically: when a second maintainer onboards post-2026-07-21 escalation review, .scp/rule-config.yaml would be modifiable by any maintainer without the CODEOWNERS gate, creating a bypass surface for expired-config suppression. The gap also breaks the estate's analogy with ADOPT-001 §12.3 (adopter repos are expected to protect .scp/ as a governance artifact).","mitigation":"Add '.scp/** @jrnb2024' to CODEOWNERS before the /CODEOWNERS self-protection last line (per the ORDERING INVARIANT: specific rules go before the final self-protection rule). This is a one-line CODEOWNERS addition. Also add a comment citing the release-gate expired-config check as the rationale, consistent with the CODEOWNERS file's documentation pattern. This is the most urgent fix among the MAJ findings — it is a gap that grows in severity as the number of maintainers grows."},{"id":"MAJ-SAFE-004","severity":"MAJ","claim":"policies/deprecations.yaml can be tampered in two ways that bypass the deprecation-ramp gate without triggering any validation error: (a) changing announced_release from a same-major version to a prior-major version converts a same-major minor-delta violation (delta=0, blocked) into the 'major-bump removal accepted' path (ann_major == cand_major-1, always allowed), silently bypassing the one-release window; (b) changing target_release to a future tag removes the entry from the candidate filter for the current cut, allowing a surface to be removed from source without any ramp-compliance check. Both vectors require a CODEOWNERS-gated PR (policies/** @jrnb2024) and are self-mergeable only in single-operator mode.","evidence":"release-gate.yml lines 173-194 (Check deprecation-ramp invariant): the same-major check at lines 173-181 enforces cand_minor - ann_minor >= 1. The major-bump path at lines 182-185: 'elif ann_major == cand_major - 1: pass' — unconditionally accepted, no further checks. The schema at schemas/deprecations.schema.json validates format (^v[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+$) and field presence but does NOT validate semantic consistency between announced_release, target_release, and the actual deprecation history. Vector (a): attacker changes announced_release from v1.0.0 to v0.9.0 for a same-release entry (both v1.x.x) — ann_major(0) == cand_major(1)-1 → accepted. Vector (b): attacker changes target_release from v1.1.0 to v1.2.0 — the entry is filtered out at line 163 (target != candidate) for the v1.1.0 cut, and the surface is silently removed from source without enforcement. In single-operator mode the CODEOWNERS gate is self-merge bus-factor-1.","impact":"Vector (a): a surface that was only announced in the same release as its removal (zero deprecation window) can be removed under the guise of a major-bump removal. Adopters who pinned at the announcement release get no deprecation warning window — the surface vanishes at the next tag-cut. This directly violates the one-release ramp invariant from VERSIONING.md (ii). Vector (b): a surface is removed from source without any matching deprecations.yaml enforcement — the gate is bypassed entirely for that removal. Both vectors are constrained to CODEOWNERS-protected PR paths and are primarily a bus-factor-1 concern at v1.0.0. They become more significant when a second maintainer onboards and an insider-threat model is active.","mitigation":"(1) For vector (a): add a cross-validation check that when ann_major == cand_major-1, the entry's announced_release also belongs to a prior shipped tag (not a synthetic prior-major claim). Practically: emit a warning annotation (not a blocking error) when ann_major < cand_major-1 OR when a major-bump path entry's announced_release is within 0 minors of the cand_major transition — leave the final block as an error for structural inconsistency as it already is. (2) For vector (b): add a check that warns when a deprecations.yaml entry whose announced_release major == cand_major exists but target_release != candidate (i.e., the surface was announced in this major cycle but scheduled for a future tag — emit an advisory annotation so the operator can verify the postponement is intentional). These are advisory improvements; the primary mitigation remains CODEOWNERS-gated review of policies/deprecations.yaml."},{"id":"MIN-SAFE-005","severity":"MIN","claim":"The expired-config check in release-gate.yml uses datetime.date.today() with strict less-than comparison (expires < today), while the equivalent check in policy-check.yml uses timezone-aware datetime.now(timezone.utc) with >= comparison. On the expiry day itself (UTC), release-gate considers a date-only expires_at entry NOT expired (strict <), but policy-check considers the same entry expired (the whole day has begun). This creates a one-day window where policy-check emits an expired-rule-config warning at PR time but release-gate allows the tag cut.","evidence":"release-gate.yml line 230: 'today = datetime.date.today()'; line 247: 'if expires < today:' (strict less-than — on expiry day: expires(2026-05-01) < today(2026-05-01) is FALSE, entry not flagged). policy-check.yml lines 877-901 (Emit expired-rule-config one-release warning): line 877: 'now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)'; line 901 area: compares datetime, so on 2026-05-01 the full datetime 2026-05-01T00:00:00+00:00 < datetime.now() is TRUE after midnight UTC. GitHub-hosted runners default to UTC so today() == UTC date; the semantic gap is one calendar day (the expiry day itself), not a timezone mismatch. The inconsistency is reproducible on any date where expires_at equals the runner date.","impact":"An expired rule-config entry on its exact expiry day will be warned about at PR time (policy-check.yml) but not blocked at tag-cut time (release-gate.yml). An operator who pushes a tag on the exact expiry day bypasses the release-gate expired-config check for that day. The window is narrow (24h at most) but the inconsistency undermines the claimed gate semantics. In practice the operator would need to time a tag push precisely to the expiry day to exploit this gap.","mitigation":"Standardise the comparison in release-gate.yml to match policy-check.yml's timezone-aware datetime approach: replace 'today = datetime.date.today()' + date comparison with 'today = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).date()' and keep 'if expires < today' — this correctly flags entries where expires_at is strictly before today UTC, consistent with the policy-check.yml semantic that treats the expiry date itself as expired. One-line change in the release-gate expired-config check."},{"id":"MIN-SAFE-006","severity":"MIN","claim":"The pyyaml and jsonschema packages installed by the 'Install pyyaml + jsonschema (lockfile-pinned)' step are version-only pinned (pyyaml==6.0.3, jsonschema==4.25.1) without --require-hashes. A PyPI compromise or mirror substitution for either package version would not be detected. This is inconsistent with the OPA/Conftest/Regal SHA256 lockfile pattern established in policy-check.yml.","evidence":"release-gate.yml line 78: 'python3 -m pip install --quiet --user \"pyyaml==6.0.3\" \"jsonschema==4.25.1\"'. No --require-hashes flag. The comment at line 76 references 'lockfile-pinned' but the scp-policy-check.lock (which contains SHA256 hashes for binary tools) covers OPA/Conftest/Regal only — not PyPI packages. policy-check.yml line 627-637 (Ensure caller-data dependencies) also installs pyyaml and jsonschema with version-only pins, establishing this as a pre-existing pattern; 020H.3 inherits it. There is no pip lock file (requirements.txt with hashes) for the Python packages used by the workflow steps.","impact":"If pyyaml or jsonschema at the pinned versions were replaced by a malicious package on PyPI (typosquatting, compromised account, or index poisoning), the workflow steps that parse YAML or validate JSON schema would execute attacker-controlled code on the GitHub Actions runner. The parse+validate steps touch policies/deprecations.yaml and schemas/deprecations.schema.json — a malicious parser could produce false validation results. Severity is MIN because PyPI index poisoning for pinned packages requires an attacker to compromise the PyPI account that published those specific versions, which is harder than a package rename attack.","mitigation":"Add a pip hash-check mechanism: generate a requirements.txt with hashes via 'pip download --dest /tmp pyyaml==6.0.3 jsonschema==4.25.1 && pip hash /tmp/pyyaml*.whl /tmp/jsonschema*.whl' and embed the hashes. Then install with 'pip install --require-hashes -r requirements.txt'. Alternatively, vendor the Python wheels under vendor/python/ with SHA256 verification matching the scp-policy-check.lock pattern. This aligns Python dependency verification with the OPA/Conftest/Regal lockfile posture. Note: this finding also applies to policy-check.yml's pip installs and should be fixed there in the same pass."},{"id":"nit-SAFE-007","severity":"nit","claim":"The concurrency group expression 'release-gate-${{ github.ref || github.event.inputs.dry_run_tag }}' for workflow_dispatch invocations never uses the dry_run_tag value. github.ref is always set for workflow_dispatch (it resolves to the branch the dispatch was triggered from, typically refs/heads/main). The || branch is dead code. All workflow_dispatch dry-run invocations share the same group 'release-gate-refs/heads/main' regardless of which dry_run_tag they evaluate, causing unnecessary serialization of concurrent dry-run evaluations.","evidence":"release-gate.yml lines 54-56: concurrency group definition. GitHub Actions documentation: for workflow_dispatch events, github.ref is the branch or tag ref from which the workflow was dispatched (default: the repository default branch, refs/heads/main). It is always a non-empty string. The || operator short-circuits when the left side is truthy; github.event.inputs.dry_run_tag is never evaluated. Two operators simultaneously dry-running v1.1.0 and v1.2.0 evaluations would serialize on the same group — cancel-in-progress: false means the second queues, not cancels.","impact":"Operational annoyance only — dry-run evaluations unnecessarily serialize. No security bypass surface. A dry-run for v1.2.0 queued behind v1.1.0 evaluation does not cross-contaminate results (each run reads its own CANDIDATE_TAG from the step output). The serialization wastes wall-clock time but produces correct results.","mitigation":"Change the concurrency group to 'release-gate-${{ github.event_name == \"push\" && github.ref || inputs.dry_run_tag }}'. This uses github.ref for push:tags events and inputs.dry_run_tag for workflow_dispatch events, ensuring each dry-run evaluation gets a distinct concurrency group."},{"id":"nit-SAFE-008","severity":"nit","claim":"The DISPATCH-NOTE 'Out of scope' section does not disclose that the push:tags trigger fires after the tag exists on the remote, making the workflow an observer/annotator rather than a pre-emptive gate. Per VERSIONING.md §4.3 disclosure contract, limitations on gate enforcement should be disclosed in the slice's dispatch note.","evidence":"DISPATCH-NOTE.md lines 72-87 ('Out of scope / forward-looking'): covers adopter-side rule-config expiry, deprecation announcement linter, release-notes auto-generation. No entry for 'post-push observation-only limitation' or 'dry_run is the real pre-flight'. VERSIONING.md lines 130-141 (Machine enforcement subsection) does document the dry_run guidance but does not disclose the post-push timing. The DISPATCH-NOTE's acceptance criterion (iii) (line 48-60) describes 'All refusals emit ::error::title=SCP-EREL-001' without noting these refusals are post-hoc.","impact":"Future maintainers reading the dispatch note for this slice will not see the post-push limitation documented, perpetuating the 'refuses the tag-cut' misconception. This is a documentation gap that compounds CRIT-SAFE-001 without introducing a new attack surface.","mitigation":"Add a bullet to DISPATCH-NOTE 'Out of scope' section: 'Post-push enforcement model: the push:tags trigger fires after the tag exists on the remote; the gate annotates violations but cannot prevent the tag from being created. The workflow_dispatch dry_run path is the intended pre-flight mechanism. Documented in VERSIONING.md \"Machine enforcement\" subsection. Recovery for erroneous tag pushes: see docs/security/branch-protection.md \"Bad-tag recovery\" (to be added per MAJ-SAFE-002 mitigation).'"}],"self_reported_concerns":["CRIT-SAFE-001 (post-push TOCTOU) is architecturally non-negotiable — GitHub Actions on push:tags cannot intercept the push. The finding is about documentation accuracy, not a workflow code defect. The claim that the dry_run pre-flight is 'the actual enforcement' is correct and defensible; the issue is that neither VERSIONING.md nor the workflow header makes this clear. The fix is documentation-only and does not require a code change to the gate logic.","MAJ-SAFE-002 (immutable bad tags) is a consequence of the interlock between D-030's tag-protection ruleset and the post-push workflow — two independently-correct decisions that compose into an undocumented failure mode. The recommended mitigation (document recovery procedure) is sufficient for v1.0.0; a stronger mitigation would be a tag-protection ruleset bypass procedure document, but that is a governance document change, not a code change.","The single-operator bus-factor-1 mode acknowledged throughout (D-033, D-031) means MAJ-SAFE-004's deprecations.yaml tamper vectors are self-mergeable. I am not treating this as a blocker because the single-operator acknowledgement is explicit estate doctrine for v1.0.0 — the finding is scoped to 'when a second maintainer onboards'. However, the .scp/** CODEOWNERS gap (MAJ-SAFE-003) should be fixed now pre-emptively per the established CODEOWNERS pattern of covering paths before they are created (see CODEOWNERS line 55-56 vendor/** comment: 'vendor/ does not yet exist but rules reference it as offline-CI fallback').","I did not find evidence of HMAC, flock, symlink, or kernel-residency attack surfaces in this slice — it is a pure Python/YAML/schema workflow with no signing keys, no lock files, no file-system concurrency, and no kernel-level operations. The attack surface is bounded to: (1) input data (deprecations.yaml, rule-config.yaml); (2) workflow trigger timing; (3) pip dependency supply chain; (4) CODEOWNERS coverage gaps."]}

findings.claim: The workflow fires on push:tags AFTER the tag has been pushed to the remote. GitHub Actions cannot block a push:tags event — the tag already exists on the remote when the first workflow step runs. The claim in the workflow header ('Refuses a tag-cut on v*') and in VERSIONING.md ('Machine enforcement: ...refuses the tag-cut (SCP-EREL-001)') is architecturally false. The workflow can annotate and fail the run, but the tag is live, the release is visible, and any adopter who fetches the tag immediately after push receives the non-compliant release. The workflow_dispatch dry_run path is the real pre-flight mechanism, but operator discipline is the only enforcement — nothing in the system prevents skipping the dry_run before tagging.
findings.evidence: release-gate.yml lines 35-38: trigger is 'push: tags: ["v*"]'. GitHub's push:tags event fires after the ref has been created on the remote, after which it cannot be cancelled by a workflow. lines 96-108 (Resolve candidate tag): tag is extracted from GITHUB_REF which already reflects the live remote state. VERSIONING.md line 130-131: 'Machine enforcement: .github/workflows/release-gate.yml runs on every push: tags: ["v*"] ...It refuses the tag-cut (SCP-EREL-001)'. DISPATCH-NOTE.md acceptance criterion (iii): 'All refusals emit ::error::title=SCP-EREL-001'. Neither document acknowledges that the refusal annotation is post-hoc, not pre-emptive. The only pre-emptive path is the operator voluntarily running 'gh workflow run release-gate.yml -f dry_run_tag=v1.1.0' before tagging — VERSIONING.md documents this guidance at line 141 but there is no machine enforcement of the discipline.
findings.impact: An operator (or attacker with push-to-tags access) who skips the dry_run pre-flight and pushes a tag that violates the deprecation ramp gets: the tag exists on the remote, the workflow fails and emits SCP-EREL-001 annotations, and adopters who fetch the tag within the window between tag push and workflow-fail notification receive the non-compliant release. The failure notification is a GitHub Actions email/notification, not a blocking gate. Adopter repos with Renovate configured to watch this tag series will see the tag and may open an upgrade PR. The documentation misleads adopters (and future maintainers) about the strength of the enforcement guarantee, causing over-reliance on a property the mechanism does not provide.
findings.mitigation: (1) Correct VERSIONING.md and the release-gate.yml header comment to state accurately: the gate detects and annotates ramp violations; it does not prevent the tag from being created. The pre-emptive enforcement is the dry_run discipline. (2) Promote the dry_run pre-flight to a documented mandatory step in VERSIONING.md's 'Deprecation ramp' section alongside the tag-cut instruction — 'Before cutting any v* tag, ALWAYS run: gh workflow run release-gate.yml -f dry_run_tag=<tag>; wait for the run to complete with exit 0 before pushing the tag.' (3) Document the recovery procedure for a bad tag (see CRIT-SAFE-001 + MAJ-SAFE-002 for the interlock with tag-protection). These are documentation changes only; no workflow code change is needed for this finding. The enforcement model is defensible as long as the claim matches reality.

findings.claim: The D-030 tag-protection ruleset (scp-tag-protection-v) blocks deletion, non_fast_forward, and update on v* tags with bypass_actors:[] and enforcement:active. This means even the repo admin cannot delete a tag once created. If an operator erroneously pushes a tag that violates the ramp (e.g., skipped the dry_run pre-flight), the release-gate workflow correctly fails and annotates the violation, but the bad tag CANNOT be deleted to contain the damage. There is no documented recovery path for this scenario.
findings.evidence: branch-protection.md lines 113-127: scp-tag-protection-v ruleset; 'deletion / non_fast_forward / update blocked'; 'bypass_actors: []' (all actors including admin blocked). docs/DECISIONS.md D-030: 'a single GitHub admin (@jrnb2024) can disable these via repo Settings; quarterly review cadence'. release-gate.yml has no step that attempts tag deletion (it lacks write permissions: permissions.contents=read at line 47). The workflow cannot delete the tag even if it wanted to. No step in any workflow file creates an issue, posts a comment, or takes recovery action on violation detection — the only output is ::error:: annotations and a non-zero exit code. DISPATCH-NOTE.md 'Out of scope' section does not mention the bad-tag-is-permanent scenario.
findings.impact: A tag-protection + post-push workflow creates a compound failure mode: (1) operator pushes v1.1.0 while skipping dry_run; (2) workflow fails, annotates ramp violation; (3) tag v1.1.0 exists, is visible to adopters, Renovate opens upgrade PRs; (4) operator cannot delete v1.1.0 without first disabling the ruleset via GitHub Settings; (5) there is no documented procedure for step (4), nor an acknowledgement that it is required. This scenario is made more likely by the misleading 'refuses the tag-cut' documentation (CRIT-SAFE-001) — an operator who believes the gate is pre-emptive may not think to run dry_run. The D-030 ruleset design rationale (preventing accidental force-push) is sound in isolation, but its interaction with the post-push gate is undocumented.
findings.mitigation: (1) Add a 'Bad-tag recovery procedure' subsection to VERSIONING.md and docs/security/branch-protection.md: 'If a tag is pushed that fails the release-gate check: (a) do NOT attempt to delete or force-push the tag — it is immutable per D-030; (b) cut a corrected v<X>.<Y+1>.0 (next minor) that satisfies the ramp; the bad tag remains but is superseded; (c) add a release note on the bad tag's GitHub release page documenting the violation and pointing to the corrected tag.' (2) Consider documenting the temporary-ruleset-disable path as an emergency escape: 'In exceptional cases where tag deletion is required, the operator must file a D-NNN decision before disabling the ruleset, perform the deletion, re-enable the ruleset, and record the D-NNN in the next quarterly branch-protection review.' No workflow code change needed.

findings.claim: .scp/** is absent from CODEOWNERS. The release-gate workflow's expired-config check at lines 213-258 reads .scp/rule-config.yaml when present. Once any SCP-self rule-config is added (currently absent, so the check is silently skipped), the file becomes load-bearing for the gate: an entry with disable:true and expires_at in the future could suppress a policy rule at tag-cut time. Without CODEOWNERS coverage, a PR adding or modifying .scp/rule-config.yaml is not routed to @jrnb2024 for mandatory review.
findings.evidence: CODEOWNERS full file reviewed: paths covered include policies/**, schemas/**, lib/**, .github/**, tests/**, renovate/**, scripts/**, vendor/**, version-manifest.json, /CODEOWNERS, docs/CODEOWNERS, and several docs/** subtrees. No .scp/** or .scp/rule-config.yaml entry exists. release-gate.yml line 213: 'if [ ! -f .scp/rule-config.yaml ]; then echo ".scp/rule-config.yaml absent on SCP repo; expired-config check skipped"; exit 0; fi'. policy-check.yml SCP_RULE_CONFIG_PATH defaults to .scp/rule-config.yaml (line 35). schema at schemas/rule-config.schema.json is covered by schemas/** but the data file at .scp/ is not. The CODEOWNERS header comment (lines 1-31) shows extensive reasoning about why each path was added; .scp/** is not mentioned, suggesting it was overlooked rather than intentionally excluded.
findings.impact: If .scp/rule-config.yaml is added to the SCP repo (a legitimate future action as SCP self-dogfoods rule governance), any subsequent PR that modifies it to extend expires_at dates, add new disable entries, or remove existing entries can be merged without @jrnb2024 CODEOWNERS review in single-operator mode (though in single-operator mode all merges are self-approved). More critically: when a second maintainer onboards post-2026-07-21 escalation review, .scp/rule-config.yaml would be modifiable by any maintainer without the CODEOWNERS gate, creating a bypass surface for expired-config suppression. The gap also breaks the estate's analogy with ADOPT-001 §12.3 (adopter repos are expected to protect .scp/ as a governance artifact).
findings.mitigation: Add '.scp/** @jrnb2024' to CODEOWNERS before the /CODEOWNERS self-protection last line (per the ORDERING INVARIANT: specific rules go before the final self-protection rule). This is a one-line CODEOWNERS addition. Also add a comment citing the release-gate expired-config check as the rationale, consistent with the CODEOWNERS file's documentation pattern. This is the most urgent fix among the MAJ findings — it is a gap that grows in severity as the number of maintainers grows.

findings.claim: policies/deprecations.yaml can be tampered in two ways that bypass the deprecation-ramp gate without triggering any validation error: (a) changing announced_release from a same-major version to a prior-major version converts a same-major minor-delta violation (delta=0, blocked) into the 'major-bump removal accepted' path (ann_major == cand_major-1, always allowed), silently bypassing the one-release window; (b) changing target_release to a future tag removes the entry from the candidate filter for the current cut, allowing a surface to be removed from source without any ramp-compliance check. Both vectors require a CODEOWNERS-gated PR (policies/** @jrnb2024) and are self-mergeable only in single-operator mode.
findings.evidence: release-gate.yml lines 173-194 (Check deprecation-ramp invariant): the same-major check at lines 173-181 enforces cand_minor - ann_minor >= 1. The major-bump path at lines 182-185: 'elif ann_major == cand_major - 1: pass' — unconditionally accepted, no further checks. The schema at schemas/deprecations.schema.json validates format (^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$) and field presence but does NOT validate semantic consistency between announced_release, target_release, and the actual deprecation history. Vector (a): attacker changes announced_release from v1.0.0 to v0.9.0 for a same-release entry (both v1.x.x) — ann_major(0) == cand_major(1)-1 → accepted. Vector (b): attacker changes target_release from v1.1.0 to v1.2.0 — the entry is filtered out at line 163 (target != candidate) for the v1.1.0 cut, and the surface is silently removed from source without enforcement. In single-operator mode the CODEOWNERS gate is self-merge bus-factor-1.
findings.impact: Vector (a): a surface that was only announced in the same release as its removal (zero deprecation window) can be removed under the guise of a major-bump removal. Adopters who pinned at the announcement release get no deprecation warning window — the surface vanishes at the next tag-cut. This directly violates the one-release ramp invariant from VERSIONING.md (ii). Vector (b): a surface is removed from source without any matching deprecations.yaml enforcement — the gate is bypassed entirely for that removal. Both vectors are constrained to CODEOWNERS-protected PR paths and are primarily a bus-factor-1 concern at v1.0.0. They become more significant when a second maintainer onboards and an insider-threat model is active.
findings.mitigation: (1) For vector (a): add a cross-validation check that when ann_major == cand_major-1, the entry's announced_release also belongs to a prior shipped tag (not a synthetic prior-major claim). Practically: emit a warning annotation (not a blocking error) when ann_major < cand_major-1 OR when a major-bump path entry's announced_release is within 0 minors of the cand_major transition — leave the final block as an error for structural inconsistency as it already is. (2) For vector (b): add a check that warns when a deprecations.yaml entry whose announced_release major == cand_major exists but target_release != candidate (i.e., the surface was announced in this major cycle but scheduled for a future tag — emit an advisory annotation so the operator can verify the postponement is intentional). These are advisory improvements; the primary mitigation remains CODEOWNERS-gated review of policies/deprecations.yaml.

findings.claim: The expired-config check in release-gate.yml uses datetime.date.today() with strict less-than comparison (expires < today), while the equivalent check in policy-check.yml uses timezone-aware datetime.now(timezone.utc) with >= comparison. On the expiry day itself (UTC), release-gate considers a date-only expires_at entry NOT expired (strict <), but policy-check considers the same entry expired (the whole day has begun). This creates a one-day window where policy-check emits an expired-rule-config warning at PR time but release-gate allows the tag cut.
findings.evidence: release-gate.yml line 230: 'today = datetime.date.today()'; line 247: 'if expires < today:' (strict less-than — on expiry day: expires(2026-05-01) < today(2026-05-01) is FALSE, entry not flagged). policy-check.yml lines 877-901 (Emit expired-rule-config one-release warning): line 877: 'now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)'; line 901 area: compares datetime, so on 2026-05-01 the full datetime 2026-05-01T00:00:00+00:00 < datetime.now() is TRUE after midnight UTC. GitHub-hosted runners default to UTC so today() == UTC date; the semantic gap is one calendar day (the expiry day itself), not a timezone mismatch. The inconsistency is reproducible on any date where expires_at equals the runner date.
findings.impact: An expired rule-config entry on its exact expiry day will be warned about at PR time (policy-check.yml) but not blocked at tag-cut time (release-gate.yml). An operator who pushes a tag on the exact expiry day bypasses the release-gate expired-config check for that day. The window is narrow (24h at most) but the inconsistency undermines the claimed gate semantics. In practice the operator would need to time a tag push precisely to the expiry day to exploit this gap.
findings.mitigation: Standardise the comparison in release-gate.yml to match policy-check.yml's timezone-aware datetime approach: replace 'today = datetime.date.today()' + date comparison with 'today = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).date()' and keep 'if expires < today' — this correctly flags entries where expires_at is strictly before today UTC, consistent with the policy-check.yml semantic that treats the expiry date itself as expired. One-line change in the release-gate expired-config check.

findings.claim: The pyyaml and jsonschema packages installed by the 'Install pyyaml + jsonschema (lockfile-pinned)' step are version-only pinned (pyyaml==6.0.3, jsonschema==4.25.1) without --require-hashes. A PyPI compromise or mirror substitution for either package version would not be detected. This is inconsistent with the OPA/Conftest/Regal SHA256 lockfile pattern established in policy-check.yml.
findings.evidence: release-gate.yml line 78: 'python3 -m pip install --quiet --user "pyyaml==6.0.3" "jsonschema==4.25.1"'. No --require-hashes flag. The comment at line 76 references 'lockfile-pinned' but the scp-policy-check.lock (which contains SHA256 hashes for binary tools) covers OPA/Conftest/Regal only — not PyPI packages. policy-check.yml line 627-637 (Ensure caller-data dependencies) also installs pyyaml and jsonschema with version-only pins, establishing this as a pre-existing pattern; 020H.3 inherits it. There is no pip lock file (requirements.txt with hashes) for the Python packages used by the workflow steps.
findings.impact: If pyyaml or jsonschema at the pinned versions were replaced by a malicious package on PyPI (typosquatting, compromised account, or index poisoning), the workflow steps that parse YAML or validate JSON schema would execute attacker-controlled code on the GitHub Actions runner. The parse+validate steps touch policies/deprecations.yaml and schemas/deprecations.schema.json — a malicious parser could produce false validation results. Severity is MIN because PyPI index poisoning for pinned packages requires an attacker to compromise the PyPI account that published those specific versions, which is harder than a package rename attack.
findings.mitigation: Add a pip hash-check mechanism: generate a requirements.txt with hashes via 'pip download --dest /tmp pyyaml==6.0.3 jsonschema==4.25.1 && pip hash /tmp/pyyaml*.whl /tmp/jsonschema*.whl' and embed the hashes. Then install with 'pip install --require-hashes -r requirements.txt'. Alternatively, vendor the Python wheels under vendor/python/ with SHA256 verification matching the scp-policy-check.lock pattern. This aligns Python dependency verification with the OPA/Conftest/Regal lockfile posture. Note: this finding also applies to policy-check.yml's pip installs and should be fixed there in the same pass.

findings.claim: The concurrency group expression 'release-gate-${{ github.ref || github.event.inputs.dry_run_tag }}' for workflow_dispatch invocations never uses the dry_run_tag value. github.ref is always set for workflow_dispatch (it resolves to the branch the dispatch was triggered from, typically refs/heads/main). The || branch is dead code. All workflow_dispatch dry-run invocations share the same group 'release-gate-refs/heads/main' regardless of which dry_run_tag they evaluate, causing unnecessary serialization of concurrent dry-run evaluations.
findings.evidence: release-gate.yml lines 54-56: concurrency group definition. GitHub Actions documentation: for workflow_dispatch events, github.ref is the branch or tag ref from which the workflow was dispatched (default: the repository default branch, refs/heads/main). It is always a non-empty string. The || operator short-circuits when the left side is truthy; github.event.inputs.dry_run_tag is never evaluated. Two operators simultaneously dry-running v1.1.0 and v1.2.0 evaluations would serialize on the same group — cancel-in-progress: false means the second queues, not cancels.
findings.impact: Operational annoyance only — dry-run evaluations unnecessarily serialize. No security bypass surface. A dry-run for v1.2.0 queued behind v1.1.0 evaluation does not cross-contaminate results (each run reads its own CANDIDATE_TAG from the step output). The serialization wastes wall-clock time but produces correct results.
findings.mitigation: Change the concurrency group to 'release-gate-${{ github.event_name == "push" && github.ref || inputs.dry_run_tag }}'. This uses github.ref for push:tags events and inputs.dry_run_tag for workflow_dispatch events, ensuring each dry-run evaluation gets a distinct concurrency group.

findings.claim: The DISPATCH-NOTE 'Out of scope' section does not disclose that the push:tags trigger fires after the tag exists on the remote, making the workflow an observer/annotator rather than a pre-emptive gate. Per VERSIONING.md §4.3 disclosure contract, limitations on gate enforcement should be disclosed in the slice's dispatch note.
findings.evidence: DISPATCH-NOTE.md lines 72-87 ('Out of scope / forward-looking'): covers adopter-side rule-config expiry, deprecation announcement linter, release-notes auto-generation. No entry for 'post-push observation-only limitation' or 'dry_run is the real pre-flight'. VERSIONING.md lines 130-141 (Machine enforcement subsection) does document the dry_run guidance but does not disclose the post-push timing. The DISPATCH-NOTE's acceptance criterion (iii) (line 48-60) describes 'All refusals emit ::error::title=SCP-EREL-001' without noting these refusals are post-hoc.
findings.impact: Future maintainers reading the dispatch note for this slice will not see the post-push limitation documented, perpetuating the 'refuses the tag-cut' misconception. This is a documentation gap that compounds CRIT-SAFE-001 without introducing a new attack surface.
findings.mitigation: Add a bullet to DISPATCH-NOTE 'Out of scope' section: 'Post-push enforcement model: the push:tags trigger fires after the tag exists on the remote; the gate annotates violations but cannot prevent the tag from being created. The workflow_dispatch dry_run path is the intended pre-flight mechanism. Documented in VERSIONING.md "Machine enforcement" subsection. Recovery for erroneous tag pushes: see docs/security/branch-protection.md "Bad-tag recovery" (to be added per MAJ-SAFE-002 mitigation).'

self_reported_concerns: CRIT-SAFE-001 (post-push TOCTOU) is architecturally non-negotiable — GitHub Actions on push:tags cannot intercept the push. The finding is about documentation accuracy, not a workflow code defect. The claim that the dry_run pre-flight is 'the actual enforcement' is correct and defensible; the issue is that neither VERSIONING.md nor the workflow header makes this clear. The fix is documentation-only and does not require a code change to the gate logic.

MAJ-SAFE-002 (immutable bad tags) is a consequence of the interlock between D-030's tag-protection ruleset and the post-push workflow — two independently-correct decisions that compose into an undocumented failure mode. The recommended mitigation (document recovery procedure) is sufficient for v1.0.0; a stronger mitigation would be a tag-protection ruleset bypass procedure document, but that is a governance document change, not a code change.

The single-operator bus-factor-1 mode acknowledged throughout (D-033, D-031) means MAJ-SAFE-004's deprecations.yaml tamper vectors are self-mergeable. I am not treating this as a blocker because the single-operator acknowledgement is explicit estate doctrine for v1.0.0 — the finding is scoped to 'when a second maintainer onboards'. However, the .scp/** CODEOWNERS gap (MAJ-SAFE-003) should be fixed now pre-emptively per the established CODEOWNERS pattern of covering paths before they are created (see CODEOWNERS line 55-56 vendor/** comment: 'vendor/ does not yet exist but rules reference it as offline-CI fallback').

I did not find evidence of HMAC, flock, symlink, or kernel-residency attack surfaces in this slice — it is a pure Python/YAML/schema workflow with no signing keys, no lock files, no file-system concurrency, and no kernel-level operations. The attack surface is bounded to: (1) input data (deprecations.yaml, rule-config.yaml); (2) workflow trigger timing; (3) pip dependency supply chain; (4) CODEOWNERS coverage gaps.
structured_review.summary: Slice 020H.3 introduces 1 CRIT, 3 MAJ, 2 MIN, and 2 nit safety/bypass findings. CRIT-SAFE-001: the workflow fires on push:tags — the tag already exists on the remote when the workflow starts. The workflow cannot prevent the tag from existing; it can only annotate and fail the run. Both the workflow header ('Refuses a tag-cut on v*') and VERSIONING.md ('the gate refuses a tag-cut') make an architecturally false claim about the security property. The dry_run workflow_dispatch is the real pre-flight but operator discipline is the only enforcement — nothing prevents skipping it. MAJ-SAFE-002 (compounding): the D-030 tag-protection ruleset blocks deletion/update with bypass_actors:[], so a bad tag that the workflow correctly annotates as violating the ramp CANNOT be deleted even by the admin. The bad tag is permanent on the remote and adopters who fetch it get the bad release — there is no documented recovery path. MAJ-SAFE-003: .scp/** is absent from CODEOWNERS; if a future SCP-self rule-config.yaml is added it becomes load-bearing for the release gate's expired-config check but is unprotected, allowing it to be merged without CODEOWNERS-gated review. MAJ-SAFE-004: deprecations.yaml can be tampered in two ways — (a) changing announced_release to a prior-major version converts a same-major ramp violation (0 minor delta) into the 'major-bump removal accepted' fast path, silently bypassing the one-release window; (b) changing target_release to a future tag removes the entry from the candidate filter for the current cut, letting a surface be removed with no ramp check applied. Both are CODEOWNERS-protected but self-mergeable in single-operator mode. MIN-SAFE-005: the expired-config check uses datetime.date.today() with strict less-than comparison, while policy-check.yml uses timezone-aware datetime.now(timezone.utc) with >= comparison; on the expiry day itself, release-gate considers the entry NOT expired but policy-check does, creating a one-day divergence window. MIN-SAFE-006: pyyaml and jsonschema are pip-installed with version-only pins (no --require-hashes), unlike the OPA/Conftest/Regal SHA256 lockfile pattern. nit-SAFE-007: concurrency group expression for workflow_dispatch always evaluates to refs/heads/main (github.ref is always set); the || github.event.inputs.dry_run_tag branch is dead code. nit-SAFE-008: DISPATCH-NOTE 'Out of scope' section omits the post-push observation-only limitation, which should be disclosed per §4.3 disclosure contract.
